title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: the surrounding pages study a finite group E = Σ of order 8. It is an extension of μ×μ by μ, with μ = {±1}. Equivalently it is an extension of μ by Σ'' ≅ Z/4Z. It arises as a quotient of the group S_0Γ, a subgroup of a product of three copies of a profinite GL_2-type group, in the 'équation des lacets' (Grothendieck–Teichmüller / braid-relation) setting. The previous page showed Σ is non-commutative: Ext^1(−,μ) is additive, and the extension is trivial on two complementary subgroups, 1×μ and the diagonal. It also showed every element of Σ∖Σ'' has order 2.

This page:
(110) Pick any x ∈ Σ∖Σ''. Then Σ ≅ {1,x}⋉Σ'', a semidirect product. If x acted trivially, Σ would be Z/2×Z/4. Then x·u, for u ∈ Σ'' of order 4, would be an element of order 4 outside Σ''. This contradicts the fact that all order-4 elements lie in Σ''. Grothendieck calls this a 'third proof' that μ = Σ/Σ'' acts non-trivially on Σ''.
Because Aut(Z/4) = {±1}, the only non-trivial action is inversion. So the structure is determined:
(111) Σ ≅ D_4, the dihedral group of order 8.
(112) There is a privileged choice of x: τ_Σ, the image mod S_0^ΠΓ^0 of τ_{S_0Γ} = (τ,τ',τ). Here τ and τ' are the 'complex-conjugation' involutions, e.g. τ' = diag(−1,1).
(113) This gives a canonical presentation Σ = {1,τ_Σ}⋉Σ'' with Σ'' ≅ Z/4 and τ_Σ(u) = u^{-1}.
(114) The projection Σ → μ×μ is recovered from its restrictions to the two factors:
- on {1,τ_Σ} ≅ μ it is the diagonal map, τ_Σ ↦ (−1,−1);
- on Σ'' it is the unique surjection Σ'' → Σ''/2Σ'' ≅ μ, followed by an inclusion of μ into μ×μ.

The next page goes on to E_ab ≅ μ×μ. It then asks whether the pulled-back extension of Z^! by μ splits, and seeks a canonical class c attached to Gal(Q̄/Q). The purpose of the present page is just to pin down the isomorphism type and a canonical presentation of this order-8 quotient.
errors: The argument 'x·u serait d'ordre 8, ce qui est absurde' is wrong as literally written. If x (order 2) commuted with u (order 4), x·u would have order 4, not 8. The correct contradiction uses the fact from the previous page: x·u would be an element of order 4 outside Σ'', whereas all order-4 elements lie in Σ''. The '8' is either a slip or a misreading of the handwriting.
Minor: the projection Σ'' → μ×μ is only described as Σ'' → Σ''/2Σ'' ≅ μ. Which embedding of μ into μ×μ is meant (it must be complementary to the diagonal, e.g. 1×μ) is left implicit on the page.

ideas.what: A non-abelian group of order 8 with a cyclic subgroup of index 2 and all elements outside it of order 2 is the dihedral group D_4, written as a semidirect product Z/2 ⋉ Z/4 acting by inversion.
ideas.modern_name: Classification of groups of order 8; dihedral group D_4

ideas.what: Canonical choice of the splitting involution as the image of the triple of 'complex conjugations' (τ,τ',τ), giving a canonical semidirect decomposition of the finite quotient Σ of S_0Γ.
ideas.modern_name: Complex conjugation / real structure in the Grothendieck–Teichmüller and braid-group setting; canonical splitting by an involution
ideas.usually_credited_to: Unsure; GT and complex-conjugation considerations appear in Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Possibly related to La Longue Marche (1981) discussions of complex conjugation; unsure

ideas.what: Recovering the homomorphism D_4 → μ×μ (the abelianization) from its restrictions to the reflection subgroup (diagonal map) and to the rotation subgroup (mod 2 reduction).

deep.surprise_reason: The page is elementary group theory: it identifies an order-8 extension as D_4 and gives a canonical presentation. The only context-specific content is the canonical involution τ_Σ = image of (τ,τ',τ). The potentially interesting thread (a canonical Galois class c from the extension of Z^! by μ) is on the next page, not here.
transcription_corrections: The second equation label is (111), not '(110)'; the image shows (11?) with a corrected digit, and it precedes (112).
'Du du seul fait' should read 'Du seul fait que l'op. de {1,x} sur Σ'' est non triviale, elle est connue, donc la structure de Σ est déterminée'.
The order claimed for x·u looks like '8' in the handwriting. Mathematically it should be '4', an element of order 4 outside Σ''.
'S_0^{To}Γ^0' is likely 'S_0^{Π}Γ^0' (compare S_0^ΠΓ^! on the next page).
The insertion above '/d'ordre 4' reads 'u de Σ''', i.e. 'pour un élément u de Σ'' d'ordre 4'.
The first-line opening '[-...-] si' is probably a struck word ('Ainsi'?) followed by 'si Σ était donc produit'.
